title: Correct final time expression
description: Essential: The answer must provide the time of motion in the electric field, expressed as one of the two correct algebraic forms derived from the impulse-momentum theorem and kinematics.

title: Correct final speed expression
description: Essential: The answer must provide the magnitude of the exit velocity, expressed as one of the two correct algebraic forms derived from the work-energy theorem.

title: Applies work-energy theorem
description: Important: The solution must correctly relate the work done by the electric force to the change in kinetic energy, accounting for the particle's negative charge and the field's direction.

title: Applies impulse-momentum theorem
description: Important: The solution must correctly relate the impulse of the electric force to the change in the particle's momentum, using the constant force magnitude qE0.

title: Considers both exit points
description: Important: The reasoning must recognize that the particle can exit the field region at either x = d or x = -2d, leading to two possible sets of answers.

title: Correct force direction
description: Important: The solution must correctly determine the direction of the electric force on the negative charge in a positive x-direction field, leading to deceleration/acceleration in different regions.

title: Sign error in work/impulse
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the sign of the work done by the electric force or the impulse is incorrect, such as forgetting the negative charge or the displacement direction.

title: Kinematic consistency check
description: Optional: The solution may verify that the derived time and speed are consistent with constant acceleration kinematics for each possible motion.

title: Physical interpretation of results
description: Optional: The solution may discuss the physical meaning of the two cases (e.g., particle turns around or continues forward) based on initial kinetic energy.
